paragraphs.sourceText: Social isolation poses more health risks than obesity or smoking 15 cigarettes a day, according to research published by Brigham Young University. The 26 is that loneliness is a huge, if silent, risk factor.
Loneliness affects physical health in two ways. First, it produces stress hormones that can lead to many health problems. Second, people who live alone are less likely to go to the doctor 27 , to
exercise or to eat a healthy diet.

Public health experts in many countries are 28 how to address widespread loneliness in our society. Last year Britain even appointed a minister for loneliness. "Loneliness 29 almost every one of us at some point," its minister for loneliness Baroness Barran said. "It can lead to very serious health
30 for individuals who become isolated and disconnected. "

He is now supporting" 32 benches," which are public seating areas where people are encouraged to go and chat with one another. The minister is also一旦to stop public transportation from being cut in ways33 that leave people isolated.

More than one-fifth of adults in both the United States and Britain said in a 2018 34 that they often or always feel lonely. More than half of American adults are unmarried, and researchers have found that even among those who are married, 30% of relationships are 35 strained. A quarter of Americans now live alone, and as the song says, one is the loneliest number.

paragraphs.sourceText: What happens when a language has no words for nmnbers?
paragraphs.translationZh: 当一种语言没有表示数字的单词时会发生什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: N Numbers do not exist in all cultures. There are numberless hunter-gatherers in Amazonia, living along branches of the world's largest river tree. Instead of using words for precise quantities, these people rely exclusively on terms similar to "a few" or "some." In contrast, our own lives are governed by numbers. As you read this, you are likely aware of what time it is, how old you are, your checking account balance, your weight and so on. The exact numbers we think with impact everything in our lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: N 数字并不存在于所有文化中。亚马逊流域有无数的狩猎采集者，他们生活在世界上最大的河树的树枝上。这些人不使用精确数量的词语，而是完全依赖类似于“一些”或“一些”的术语。相比之下，我们自己的生活是由数字决定的。当您阅读本文时，您可能知道现在是什么时间、您的年龄、您的支票账户余额、您的体重等等。我们所思考的确切数字会影响我们生活中的一切。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) But, in a historical sense, number-conscious people like us are the unusual ones. For the bulk of our species' approximately 200,000-year lifespan, we had no means of precisely representing quantities. What's more, the 7,000 or so languages that exist today vary dramatically in how they utilize numbers.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 但是，从历史的角度来看，像我们这样有数字意识的人是不寻常的。对于我们大部分物种大约 20 万年的寿命来说，我们没有办法精确地表示数量。此外，当今存在的大约 7,000 种语言在使用数字的方式上存在巨大差异。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Speakers of anumeric, or numberless, languages offer a window into how the invention of numbers reshaped the human experience. Olltures without nwnbers, or with only one or two precise numbers, include the Munduruku and氏啦in Ar四釭血. Researchers have also studied some adults in Nicaragua who were never taught nmnber words. Without numbers, healthy human adults struggle to precisely distinguish and recall quantities as low as four. In an experiment, a researcher will place nuts into a can one at a time and then remove them one by one. The person watching is asked to signal when all the nuts have been removed. Responses suggest that anumeric people have some trouble keeping track of how many nuts remain in the can, even if there are only four or five in total.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 使用数字或无数语言的人提供了一个窗口，让我们了解数字的发明如何重塑人类的经验。没有数字或只有一两个精确数字的语言，包括《Ar四釭血》中的Munduruku和氏啦。研究人员还对尼加拉瓜的一些成年人进行了研究，他们从未被教过单词。如果没有数字，健康的成年人很难精确地区分和回忆低至四的数量。在一项实验中，研究人员会将坚果一次一个地放入罐中，然后将它们一个一个地取出。当所有螺母都被移除时，观看者被要求发出信号。回应表明，数字人们很难追踪罐头里还剩下多少坚果，即使总共只有四到五个。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) This and many other experiments have led to a simple conclusion: When people do not have number words, they struggle to make quantitative distinctions that probably seem natural to someone like you or me. W血e only a small portion of the world's languages are anumeric or nearly anumeric, they demonstrate that number words are not a human universal.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）这个实验和许多其他实验得出了一个简单的结论：当人们没有数字词时，他们很难做出数量上的区别，而这对于像你我这样的人来说可能看起来很自然。尽管世界上只有一小部分语言是数字语言或接近数字语言，但它们表明数字词并不是人类的通用语言。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) It is worth stressing that these anumeric people are cognitively (在认知方面）normal, well-adapted to the surroundings they have dominated for centuries. As a child, I spent some time living with anumeric people, the Piraha who live along the banks of the black Maici River. Like other outsiders, I was continually impressed by their superior understanding of the ecology we shared. Yet numberless people struggle with tasks that require precise discrimination between quantities. Perhaps this should be unsurprising. After all, without counting, how can someone tell whether there are, say, seven or eight coconuts (椰子）in a tree? Such seemingly straightforward distinctions become blurry through numberless eyes.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 值得强调的是，这些数字人在认知方面是正常的，能够很好地适应他们统治了几个世纪的环境。小时候，我花了一些时间与数字人一起生活，他们生活在黑色的麦西河沿岸。像其他局外人一样，他们对我们共同的生态的卓越理解给我留下了深刻的印象。然而，无数人在需要精确区分数量的任务中挣扎。也许这应该不足为奇。毕竟，没有数数，如何才能分辨出一棵树上有七个或八个椰子（椰子）？这种看似简单的区别在无数眼睛中变得模糊。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) This conclusion is echoed by work with anumeric children in industrialized societies. Prior to being spoon-fed number words, children can only approximately discriminate quantities beyond three. We must be handed the cognitive tools of numbers before we can consistently and easily recognize higher quantities. In fact, acquiring the exact meaning of number words is a painstaking process that takes children years. Initially, kids learn numbers much like they learn letters. They recognize that numbers are organized sequentially, but have little awareness of what each individual number means. With time, they start to understand that a given number represents a quantity greater by one than the number coming before it. This "successor principle" is part of the foundation of our numerical (数字的）cognition, but requires extensive practice to understand.
paragraphs.translationZh: F）这一结论与工业化社会中无数字儿童的研究相呼应。在用勺子喂数字词之前，孩子们只能大致辨别三个以上的数量。在我们能够一致且轻松地识别更高的数量之前，我们必须掌握数字的认知工具。事实上，获得数字词的确切含义是一个艰苦的过程，需要孩子们花费数年的时间。最初，孩子们学习数字就像学习字母一样。他们认识到数字是按顺序组织的，但对每个数字的含义知之甚少。随着时间的推移，他们开始明白给定的数字代表的数量比它之前的数字大一。这个“后继原理”是我们数字认知基础的一部分，但需要大量的实践才能理解。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) None of us, then, is really a "numbers person." We are not born to handle quantitative distinctions skillfully. In the absence of the cultural traditions that fill our lives with numbers from infancy, we would all struggle with even basic quantitative distinctions. Number words and their written forms transform our quantitative reasoning as they are introduced into our cognitive experience by our parents, peers and school teachers. The process seems so normal that we sometimes think of it as a natural part of growing up, but it is not. Human brains come equipped with certain quantitative instincts that are refined with age, but these instincts are very limited.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 那么，我们都不是真正的“数字人”。我们生来就不能熟练地处理数量上的区别。如果没有从婴儿时期起就让我们的生活充满数字的文化传统，我们都会在连基本的数量区别上挣扎。当数字词及其书面形式被我们的父母、同龄人和学校老师引入我们的认知经验时，它们改变了我们的定量推理。这个过程似乎很正常，以至于我们有时认为它是成长的自然组成部分，但事实并非如此。人类大脑具有某些随着年龄的增长而完善的定量本能，但这些本能非常有限。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Compared with other mammals, our numerical instincts are not as remarkable as many assume. We even share some basic instinctual quantitative reasoning with distant non-mammalian relatives like birds. Indeed, work with some other species suggests they too can refine their quantitative thought if they are introduced to the cognitive power tools we call numbers.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 与其他哺乳动物相比，我们的数字本能并不像许多人想象的那么显着。我们甚至与鸟类等远亲非哺乳动物有一些基本的本能定量推理。事实上，与其他一些物种的合作表明，如果向它们引入我们称之为数字的认知工具，它们也可以完善其定量思维。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) So, how did we ever invent "unnatural" numbers in the first place? The answer is, literally, at your fingertips. The bulk of the world's languages use base-10, base-20 or base-5 number systems. That is, these smaller numbers are the basis of larger numbers. English is a base-10 or decimal (十进制的） language, as evidenced by words like 14 ("four"+ "10") and 31 ("three" x "10" +"one"). We speak a decimal language because an ancestral tongue, proto-Indo-Buropean, was decimally based. Proto-Inda­ European was decimally oriented because, as in so many cultures, our ancestors' hands served as the gateway to the realization that "five fingers on one hand is the same as five fingers on the other. " Such momentary thoughts were represented in words and passed down across generations. This is why the word "five" in many languages is derived from the word for "hand." Most number systems, then, are the by-product of two key factors: the human capacity for language and our inclination for focusing on our hands and fingers. This manual fixation—an indirect by-product of walking upright on two legs— has helped yield numbers in most cultures, but not all.
paragraphs.translationZh: I）那么，我们最初是如何发明“非自然”数字的呢？答案就在您的指尖。世界上大部分语言都使用以 10 为基数、以 20 为基数或以 5 为基数的数字系统。也就是说，这些较小的数字是较大数字的基础。英语是一种以 10 或十进制为基础的语言，如 14（“四”+“10”）和 31（“三”x“10”+“一”）等词所证明。我们说十进制语言是因为祖先的语言，原始印度-布罗布语，是以十进制为基础的。原始印度欧洲人是以十进制为导向的，因为，就像在许多文化中一样，我们祖先的双手是实现“五”的门户。一只手上的手指与另一只手上的五个手指是一样的。”这种瞬间的想法以文字表达并代代相传。这就是为什么许多语言中的“五”一词源自“手”一词。因此，大多数数字系统都是两个关键因素的副产品：人类的语言能力和我们关注手和手指的倾向。这种手动固定——两条腿直立行走的间接副产品——在大多数文化中都有助于产生数字，但不是所有文化。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Cultures without numbers also offer insight into the cognitive influence of particular numeric traditions. Consider what time it is. Your day is ruled by minutes and seconds, but these concepts are not real in any physical sense and are nonexistent to numberless people. .Minutes and seconds are the verbal and written representations of an uncommon base-60 number system used in ancient Mesopotamia. They reside in our minds, numerical artifacts (人工制品）that not all humans inherit conceptually.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 没有数字的文化也提供了对特定数字传统的认知影响的洞察。考虑一下现在是什么时间。你的一天是由分钟和秒统治的，但这些概念在任何物理意义上都不是真实的，并且对无数人来说是不存在的。分钟和秒是古代美索不达米亚使用的不常见的 60 进制数字系统的口头和书面表示。它们存在于我们的头脑中，是并非所有人类都在概念上继承的数字制品（人工制品）。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Research on the language of numbers shows, more and more, that one of our species' key characteristics is tremendous linguistic (语言的）and cognitive diversity. If we are to truly understand how much our cognitive lives differ cross-culturally, we must continually explore the depths of our species' linguistic diversity.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 对数字语言的研究越来越多地表明，我们物种的关键特征之一是巨大的语言和认知多样性。如果我们要真正了解我们的认知生活在跨文化中有何差异，我们必须不断探索我们物种语言多样性的深度。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. It is difficult for anumeric people to keep track of the change in numbers even when the total is very small.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 即使总数很小，数字人也很难跟踪数字的变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Human numerical instincts are not so superior to those of other mammals as is generally believed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 人类的数字本能并不像人们普遍认为的那样优于其他哺乳动物。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. The author emphasizes being anumeric does not affect one's cognitive ability.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 作者强调成为数字并不影响一个人的认知能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. In the long history of mankind, humans who use numbers are a very small minority.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39、在人类漫长的历史中，使用数字的人类是极少数。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. An in-depth study of differences between human languages contributes to a true understanding of cognitive differences between cultures.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 深入研究人类语言之间的差异有助于真正理解文化之间的认知差异。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. A conclusion has been drawn from many experiments that anumeric people have a hard time distinguishing quantities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 许多实验得出的结论是，数字人很难区分数量。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Making quantitative distinctions is not an inborn skill.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 进行定量区分并不是一种与生俱来的技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Every aspect of our lives is affected by numbers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 我们生活的方方面面都受到数字的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Larger numbers are said to be built upon smaller numbers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44.据说较大的数字是建立在较小的数字之上的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. It takes great efforts for children to grasp the concept of number words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 孩子们需要付出很大的努力才能掌握数字词的概念。

paragraphs.sourceText: Sugar shocked. That describes the reaction of many Americans this week following revelations that, 50 years ago, the sugar industry paid Harvard scientists for research that shifted the focus away from
paragraphs.translationZh: 糖震惊了。这描述了本周许多美国人的反应，因为有消息称，50年前，制糖业向哈佛大学的科学家支付了研究费用，从而将人们的注意力从糖业转移到了其他地方。

paragraphs.sourceText: What might surprise consumers is just how many present-day nutrition studies are still funded by the food industry. Nutrition scholar Marion Nestle of New York University spent a year informally tracking industry-funded studies on food. "Roughly 90% of nearly 170 studies favored the sponsor's interest," Nestle tells us. Other systematic reviews support her conclusions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 可能令消费者感到惊讶的是，目前有多少营养研究仍然由食品行业资助。纽约大学的营养学者 Marion Nestle 花了一年的时间非正式地跟踪行业资助的食品研究。 “在近 170 项研究中，大约 90% 的研究都支持申办者的利益，”雀巢告诉我们。其他系统评价支持她的结论。

paragraphs.sourceText: For instance, studies funded by Welch Foods--the brand behind Welch's 100% Grape Juice-found that drinking Concord grape juice daily may boost brain function. Another, funded by Qualcer Oats, concluded, as a Daily Mail story put it, that "hot oatmeal (燕麦粥） brealdast keeps you full for longer. "
paragraphs.translationZh: 例如，由 Welch Foods（Welch 100% 葡萄汁背后的品牌）资助的研究发现，每天饮用 Concord 葡萄汁可能会增强大脑功能。另一项由 Qualcer Oats 资助的项目得出的结论是，正如《每日邮报》的一篇报道所言，“热燕麦粥可以让你更长时间保持饱腹感。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Last year, The New York Times revealed how Coca七ola was funding well-known scientists and organizations promoting a message that, in the battle against weight gain, people should pay more attention to exercise and less to what they eat and drink. paragraphs.sourceText: "It's certainly a problem that so much research in nutrition and health is funded by industry," says Bonnie Liebman, director of nutrition at the Center for Science in the Public Interest. "When the food industry pays for research, it often gets what it pays for." And what it pays for is often a pro-industry finding.
paragraphs.translationZh: “如此多的营养和健康研究都是由工业界资助的，这无疑是一个问题，”公共利益科学中心营养主任邦妮·利布曼说。 “当食品行业为研究付费时，它往往会得到回报。”而它所付出的代价往往是有利于行业的发现。

paragraphs.sourceText: Given this environment, consumers should be skeptical (怀疑的） when reading the latest finding in nutrition science and ignore the latest study that pops up on your news feed. "Rely on health experts who've reviewed all the evidence," Liebman says, pointing to the official government Dietary Guidelines,
paragraphs.translationZh: 在这种环境下，消费者在阅读营养科学的最新发现时应该持怀疑态度，并忽略新闻推送中出现的最新研究。利布曼指出，“要依靠审查过所有证据的健康专家”，他指的是官方的政府饮食指南，

paragraphs.sourceText: which are based on reviews of hundreds of studies.
